prompt.context: Your client is the mayor of Emerald City — a large, metropolitan US city (i.e., New York or Los Angeles). She has noticed that Emerald City's FDI levels — foreign direct investment — have been decreasing over the past year. The mayor wants to turn this trend around.
prompt.question: What are the main factors she should consider as causes of the decline?

clarifying_info.a: Foreign direct investment is an investment made by a firm or individual in a foreign country into businesses located in the country of interest. Generally, FDI takes place when an investor establishes foreign business operations or acquires foreign business assets (as opposed to equity purchases).

clarifying_info.q: Why does the mayor want to increase FDI?
clarifying_info.a: She is interested in the foreign income opportunities, as well as the benefits to Emerald City's population.

clarifying_info.q: What foreign entities currently invest in Emerald City?
clarifying_info.a: Foreign investors into Emerald City include firms from a broad range of markets, from mature economies such as the EU and China, to emerging economies such as Brazil and India.

clarifying_info.q: What is the goal or target?
clarifying_info.a: A $60 billion increase in FDI over the next 2 years.

clarifying_info.q: What are Emerald City's major industries (or any other question)?
clarifying_info.a: Whatever you want them to be — we don't have information on that.

exhibits.title: Emerald City FDI Sources
exhibits.shows: A table listing six foreign markets (EU, China, Canada, Russia, Brazil, India) with three columns: GDP in trillions, FDI in Emerald City expressed as a percentage of that market's GDP, and annual growth rate of that FDI.

framework: Emerald City Characteristics (Internal): growth opportunities, industry-specific factors, population growth, tax rate, transport/infrastructure
Labor (Internal): skill of labor force, wage rates, unemployment
Macroeconomic — External: mix/growth of foreign investors, strength of dollar, diversification potential, free trade/tariffs
Geopolitical/Social — External: political stability/corruption, geographical constraints
Risks (secondary): domestic political shift, integration of production/supplier sites, cannibalization of domestic investment, effect on exchange rates, environmental concerns, cultural tensions

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, the mayor wants to know what you think of her goal to increase FDI by $60 billion over 2 years. Is the goal aggressive enough?
questions.guidance: Candidates should immediately note that emerging markets (Brazil, India, Russia) have generally higher growth rates than mature ones (EU, China), consistent with the law of diminishing marginal returns. They should also highlight notable data points such as Canada's disproportionately large FDI share (10% of GDP) and Russia's high growth rate (10%). They should then estimate total expected organic growth from these six markets alone and compare it to the $60B target. The takeaway is that the $60B goal is NOT aggressive enough — organic growth from these six markets alone gets the mayor roughly 90% of the way there without any new initiatives.

math.setup: For each market: Current FDI = GDP (trillions) × FDI% × 1,000 (to get billions). Easy growth estimate over 2 years: Current FDI × Growth Rate × 2 years. Sum total growth across all markets.
math.answer: ~$54 billion in organic growth from these six markets alone, which is ~90% of the $60B target. The mayor's $60B goal is not aggressive enough; she should set a higher target, especially if she implements new growth initiatives or taps other foreign markets.

brainstorming.prompt: The mayor is interested in your overall thoughts on what increased FDI will do for her and Emerald City, as well as the risks.

categories.name: Financial Benefits
ideas: Increased investment and consumption in the local economy
Decreased unemployment as foreign firms hire local workers
Higher tax revenue for the city

categories.name: Non-Financial Benefits
ideas: Greater political stability from stronger international ties
Re-election prospects for the mayor from visible economic progress

categories.name: Regulatory Risks
ideas: US federal legislation not aligned with local goals

recommendation: FDI from these six markets alone is expected to grow by ~$54B organically — nearly 90% of the $60B target — suggesting the mayor should raise her ambition and set a higher goal

The mayor should pursue targeted initiatives (infrastructure investment, labor development, tax incentives) to attract additional FDI beyond organic growth, particularly from high-growth emerging markets
risks: Domestic political shift could reverse progress
US federal regulatory constraints may limit local FDI incentives
Cultural tensions or integration challenges with foreign firms
next_steps: Identify specific industries or zones where FDI incentives would have highest impact
Engage emerging-market investors (Brazil, India, Russia) where growth rates are highest
Develop a monitoring framework to track FDI trends quarterly and adjust strategy accordingly
